description: The Kurinji blooms once every 12 years—roughly the same odds as finding Planet X by staring at static spreadsheets. Armed with SPHEREx data, we're blinking at the universe until something moves back.
summary:
Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) sees through darkness, smoke, and dense monsoon clouds—yet single-snapshot radar images are notoriously easy to misread. Wind waves over reservoirs look like dry land, flash freezes look like disappearing meltwater, and steep mountain relief creates radar layover.

SAR Symphony transforms multi-sensor Earth observations into an AI-directed, 12-frame interactive story across six synchronized Earth signals (SAR backscatter, GPM rain, wind, surface temperature, optical NDVI, and NASA Black Marble nightlights). Paired with a 4-bit pixel-level Radar Illusion Guard and live NASA EONET + ASF DAAC Sentinel-1 search integration, the platform lets scientists, disaster responders, and students trace full cause-and-effect chains—from upstream atmospheric triggers to ground impact and human power outages—in under a minute.
details:
1. WHAT DOES IT DO AND HOW DOES IT WORK?

SAR Symphony: Dancing with Earth's Signals is an interactive multi-sensor Earth observation studio and AI-directed causal story platform. It transforms Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and five companion NASA satellite datasets into a synchronized, 5-step cause-and-effect domino story and 12-pass time-series timeline for any disaster or environmental rhythm on Earth.

While optical satellite cameras are blinded by clouds across roughly 67% of the planet—especially during monsoons, cyclones, wildfire smoke, and polar winter nights—Synthetic Aperture Radar (Sentinel-1 and NASA-ISRO NISAR) penetrates clouds, rain, and darkness by measuring microwave surface roughness and dielectric moisture. However, raw SAR imagery alone often misleads non-experts and automated thresholds: storm winds roughen floodwater so it reflects bright radar echoes (+13.5 dB) that look like dry land; flash freezes drop snow permittivity (-8.5 dB) and mimic sudden drought; and flooded vertical rice stalks create double-bounce reflections (+2.2 dB) that mimic urban buildings.

SAR Symphony solves this by synchronizing 6 complementary Earth signals onto a unified 12-pass timeline and 64x64 spatial cube:

1) SAR Backscatter (dB) - Copernicus Sentinel-1 and NASA-ISRO NISAR (via NASA ASF DAAC)

2) Precipitation Rate (mm/hr) - NASA GPM IMERG

3) Surface Wind Speed (m/s) - NASA MERRA-2 / NASA POWER / Open-Meteo

4) Land Surface Temperature (deg C) - NASA MODIS / ECOSTRESS

5) Vegetation Greenness (NDVI) - Copernicus Sentinel-2 and NASA VIIRS

6) Nighttime Lights Radiance (nW/cm2/sr) - NASA Black Marble VNP46A2

How it works step by step:

- Three Entry Modes: Users can (a) launch 5 pre-baked flagship benchmark stories for instant offline replay (Bay of Bengal Cyclone to Kandy Floods in Sri Lanka; Amazon Heat Dome to Drought and Fire in Brazil; Pacific Gradient to Lahaina Wildfire and Blackout in Maui; Mahaweli Irrigation to Rice Heartbeat in Sri Lanka; and Disko Bay Inflow to Jakobshavn Polar Glacier Surge in Greenland), (b) select live active global disasters from the real-time NASA EONET v3 feed, or (c) search any city, disaster name, or latitude/longitude coordinate to generate a live 12-pass causal story.

- Multi-Scale Interactive Story Map: A Leaflet-based geospatial canvas with live NASA GIBS WMTS satellite imagery, Dark/Satellite/Terrain basemaps, animated wind and flood-flow particle vectors, a draggable Before-vs-Peak swipe curtain, and automatic camera zoom transitions from macro synoptic triggers (upwind ocean cyclones or heat domes) down to street-level neighborhood impacts.

- 5-Step Cause-to-Effect Domino Pipeline: An AI Story Director breaks every event into 5 chronological phases (Heat/Trigger -> Wind -> Rain -> SAR Ground Change -> Human Impact), automatically activating only the 2 to 3 most relevant datasets per step so users are never overwhelmed by 6 overlapping layers.

- 4-Bit Radar Illusion Guard: A per-pixel uint16 bitmask engine cross-checks SAR backscatter against MERRA-2 wind speed, MODIS sub-zero temperature, terrain slope, and cloud fraction to automatically detect and correct four physical SAR traps: Wind-Ripple Glare (0x0001), Sub-Zero Freeze Drop (0x0002), Steep-Slope Layover (0x0004), and Cloud Obscuration of Optical Sensors (0x0008).

- Equal-Scale 6-Signal Timeline and Ask AI Director: Clicking any location on the map extracts all 6 normalized time series side by side on a synchronized chart, computes lead-lag Pearson cross-correlations (such as SAR canopy moisture dropping 21 days before optical NDVI turns brown in the Amazon), and lets users ask natural-language causal questions via the Ask AI Director (powered by deterministic statistical graph synthesis with optional Gemini 2.5 Flash enhancement).

2. WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

- Sees Through Clouds While Eliminating False Radar Alarms: Combines SAR's all-weather, day-and-night ground visibility with physical cross-checks from wind, temperature, and optical sensors so responders do not mistake wind-roughened reservoirs for dry ground or irrigated rice paddies for flood disasters.

- Reveals Early Warning Lead Times: Quantifies exact day-by-day lead-lag relationships across sensors—for example, showing a 21-day early warning of forest drought stress in radar backscatter before leaves lose greenness in optical imagery, or a 4-day upstream cyclone wind and rain buildup before river floodplain inundation.

- Connects Physical Hazards Directly to Human Impact: Integrates NASA Black Marble nighttime lights alongside weather and radar to pinpoint neighborhood power grid blackouts (-78% in Kandy, -85% in Lahaina) on the exact same timeline as the physical hazard.

- Zero-Barrier, Sub-Second Web Experience: Uses a custom binary wire format (SFP1 Little-Endian float32 + uint16 bitmask framepacks) that transfers full 12-frame multi-sensor cubes in ~3.4 MB per event, rendering at 60 FPS directly in any web browser without requiring heavy desktop GIS software (like SNAP or QGIS), API keys, or gigabyte-scale GeoTIFF downloads.

3. WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT OF THE PROJECT?

- Emergency Responders and Disaster Managers: Rapidly distinguish true floodplain inundation and landslide scars from wind-ripple radar artifacts under 88% to 100% monsoon cloud cover, and prioritize rescue dispatch by overlaying Black Marble power outage zones.

- Agricultural Planners and Farmers: Track the seasonal irrigation-to-harvest rhythm of staple crops like rice in Sri Lanka's Mahaweli Basin and detect canopy water stress weeks before visible crop wilting occurs.

- Cryosphere and Climate Researchers: Monitor glacier calving retreats and velocity surges (such as Jakobshavn Isbrae at 42 m/day) through 24-hour polar winter darkness while separating dielectric surface freeze drops from structural ice loss.

- Educators, Journalists, and Local Communities Worldwide: Democratize radar remote sensing through an interactive 60-second Guided Tour, plain-language causal explanations, CSV data exports, and full support for 8 languages (English, Sinhala, Tamil, Spanish, Hindi, Arabic with right-to-left layout, Chinese, and French).

4. WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE TO DEVELOP YOUR PROJECT?

- Coding Languages: Python 3.11 (backend data pipeline, physical modeling, statistical causality, and REST/SSE APIs), TypeScript and JavaScript (frontend interactive studio, binary decoder, and canvas rendering), HTML5, and CSS3.

- Backend Frameworks and Libraries: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic v2, NumPy, SciPy (spatial filtering and Pearson lead-lag cross-correlation), httpx (async queries to NASA/Copernicus/Open-Meteo endpoints), and pytest (48 automated unit and integration tests).

- Frontend Frameworks and Visualization Libraries: React 18, Vite, Leaflet (interactive multi-scale geospatial map, NASA GIBS WMTS tile integration, custom raster overlays, and animated vector particle canvas), Plotly.js (synchronized 6-signal time-series charts), HTML5 2D Canvas, and custom ArrayBuffer SFP1 binary framepack decoders.

- NASA and Open Science Data Sources & APIs: NASA ASF DAAC (Sentinel-1 SAR & NISAR simulated L/C-band time series), NASA GIBS WMTS (MODIS Terra, GPM IMERG, VIIRS Day/Night Band tiles), NASA GPM IMERG, NASA MERRA-2 & NASA POWER API, NASA MODIS / ECOSTRESS LST, NASA Black Marble VNP46A2, Copernicus Sentinel-2 / VIIRS NDVI, NASA EONET v3 API, and Open-Meteo Archive & Geocoding APIs.

- AI and Causality Engine: Two-tier architecture featuring a deterministic SciPy/NumPy cross-correlation and hotspot detection engine (Tier 1, 100% offline-capable) paired with optional Google Gemini 3.5 Flash API synthesis (Tier 2) for natural-language Q&A.

- Packaging and Deployment Software: Docker (single-container multi-stage build on port 7860), Git/GitHub, and standard consumer laptop hardware (no specialized GPU required).

5. HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

- Treating Earth Observation as a "Symphony" of Coupled Signals: Instead of presenting satellite datasets as isolated static layers in separate portals, we treat each sensor as an instrument in a synchronized score—where ocean heat and wind play the opening notes, rainfall and SAR radar carry the crescendo, and nighttime lights reveal the human aftermath.

- The 4-Bit Radar Illusion Guard: Rather than hiding SAR's physical ambiguities, we turned them into a core interactive teaching and verification feature. Users can toggle the Illusion Guard on and off to watch how wind-rippled water, sub-zero snow freezes, or steep slopes deceive raw radar, and how pairing NASA weather/thermal sensors exposes the truth.

- Multi-Scale Domino Storytelling with Anti-Overwhelm Decluttering: Our 5-step Domino Pipeline automatically flies the map camera from upstream synoptic causes (hundreds of kilometers away) down to local valley and street impacts while dynamically toggling only the 2 to 3 relevant sensors for each step.

- Custom SFP1 Binary Wire Format: We engineered a lightweight binary framepack format (SFP1) that packs 4D float32 data cubes alongside uint16 quality/illusion bitmasks, enabling instant scrubbing and live pixel math in the browser.

6. WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

- Cognitive Load vs. Scientific Rigor: Showing 6 satellite datasets across 12 dates (72 spatial grids) all at once overwhelms users. We designed the AI Story Director to curate 2 to 3 layers per scene and normalize all 6 series onto an equal 0-to-100% visual scale while preserving exact physical units (dB, mm/hr, m/s, deg C, NDVI, nW/cm2/sr) on hover and export.

- Physical Authenticity and Honest Resolution Boundaries: Different satellite instruments operate at different native resolutions (from 10-30 m SAR and optical to 0.1 deg IMERG rain and 0.5 deg MERRA-2 wind) and revisit cadences. We explicitly document co-registration, resampling, and physical backscatter mechanisms in our built-in Science Guide.

- Offline Reliability and Zero-Key Accessibility: Live satellite APIs can be rate-limited or unreachable in low-connectivity disaster zones. We pre-baked 5 complete flagship event archives (17.24 MB total) and built deterministic fallback synthesis so every feature works reliably offline with zero API keys required.

- Local Context and Global Inclusivity: Inspired by real monsoon flooding and agricultural cycles in our home region of Kandy and the Mahaweli Basin in Sri Lanka—and paired with global benchmarks in Maui, the Amazon, and Greenland—we built the interface to support 8 languages (including Sinhala, Tamil, and right-to-left Arabic) so communities on the front lines of climate hazards can explore NASA data in their own language.
